summary: The core is a scan-time raster design. Tiles are fetched on hdump phases, sprites are found per line into a line buffer, and colour goes through a chain of PROM lookups addressed the way the board's lookup and palette PROMs would be wired. It models several things MAME leaves out: a free-running sound timer counter, the VLM5030 address/data mux and filter-enable latch bits, edge flip-flops cleared by IRQ acknowledge, a tile priority bit, and the scroll-register readback port. No module mirrors MAME's screen_update/draw_sprites/tile_info decomposition. It is not a strict chip-per-module or gate-level reconstruction, though: much of it is generic shared jtframe/kicker infrastructure with LAYOUT parameters, so the lean is moderate.

findings.signal: PROM lookup chain instead of precomputed pens
findings.note: Tile and sprite pixels go through 256x4 lookup PROMs, then the 3 palette PROMs, addressed {pal_sel or 4'hf, nibble}. MAME instead folds the same data into indirect pen tables (ctabentry |0xf0, (j<<4)|lut) with resistor weights.
The ROM address is latched at hdump[2:0]==0 and the data captured at ==4, then shifted out one pixel per pxl_cen. The board's 8-pixel fetch cycle is reproduced, not a tilemap drawn per frame.

findings.signal: fixed-column scroll split as raster compare
findings.note: The non-scrolling score area comes from an hdump<SCRCOL (octal 060) comparison inside a per-clock scroll adder with a +1 offset and flip XOR. MAME has a loop over scroll columns 6..31 instead.

findings.signal: behaviour MAME omits: scroll readback and tile priority
findings.note: A read port at 3C30 returns the live scroll counter (vscr). Colour attribute bit 4 acts as a tile-over-sprite priority in the mixer. MAME has neither: it draws all sprites over the tilemap.

findings.signal: per-line sprite engine with line buffer and table copy
findings.note: At a fixed raster line (vrender==0x40) the sprite RAM is copied into a double-buffered table, with the byte order reordered. Each line then scans 64 entries for y-in-zone and draws into a line buffer. MAME instead draws whole sprites per frame and skips entries where sx/sy are zero, which this core does not.
The raster is a 384-clock line and 264 lines, with blanking/sync at specific counts, and V16 is taken from vdump bit 4. MAME uses an idealised 256x256 screen with zero vblank time.

findings.signal: sound board timer and VLM wiring
findings.note: The 8000 read returns bits of a free-running counter clocked by psg_cen. MAME computes it from total_cycles()/TIMER_RATE. The C000 latch also drives the A3 VLM data-source mux and the A6-A8 filter enables, which MAME marks 'don't care'. The VLM fetches its ROM through its own address/ME pins.
Both IRQs are edge-set flip-flops. The main one is cleared by the INTST latch bit, the sound one by the Z80 IORQ&M1 acknowledge. MAME uses set_input_line HOLD_LINE.
The decode follows the memory map as nested A[15:13]/A[12:11]/A[9:7]/A[6:4] cases. The latch bits (flip, INTST, OBJ CHE) match MAME's ls259 wiring, as any correct core must.
Opcode decryption is a single XOR with {A1,0,~A1,0,A3,0,~A3,0}. It is functionally identical to MAME's 4-case table (0x22/0x82/0x28/0x88) but written as wiring rather than a table.

The tile attribute bit assignments are chosen by a LAYOUT case covering seven Konami games, a reusable software-like abstraction rather than this board's netlist. It does not, however, copy MAME's tile_info expression (hflip is ~attr[6] here).
